episodes.181620: A potent thunderstorm complex developed in southwestern Tennessee and northeast Mississippi during the mid to late afternoon hours and raced east across northwestern Alabama during the late afternoon to early evening hours. This complex of strong to severe storms produced widespread wind damage and winds of 60 to 70 mph and isolated quarter inch hail. Especially hard hit was Colbert and Lauderdale counties. At least 4,000 people were without power in Florence. This complex weakened significantly as it moved towards and east of the I-65 corridor.  However, another pocket of stronger wind damage was seen in the Berlin area of Cullman county as well.
episodes.181659: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms raced west to east at 50-65 mph across north Alabama. Numerous reports of trees and power lines being knocked down were received, knocking at power to tens of thousands in north central Alabama. Injuries were reported in DeKalb County when a tree was knocked down onto a residence, collapsing it. Lightning strikes may have also sparked a grass fire or other fires. At least 21,000 utility customers in Madison County were without power.
episodes.181741: A couple of thunderstorms impacted southwest Middle Tennessee during the early evening hours of August 5, 2023. These thunderstorms were briefly severe with damaging winds causing a few trees and powerlines to fall in Lawrence County.
episodes.182568: Thunderstorms with heavy rain repeatedly moved over the same areas in Columbia, producing flash flooding.
episodes.182570: An upper level short wave passing over a very unstable airmass led to numerous severe thunderstorms, producing widespread wind damage and hail from the Central Savannah River Area up into the Midlands and Pee Dee of South Carolina.
episodes.182807: A closed 500 mb low over the Pacific Northwest opened up and shifted toward the Northern Rockies during this period. This wave, in combination with daytime heating, resulted in showers and thunderstorms across the region August 6th. Shear was meager, but was maximized locally to produce one tornado in Jefferson County. Additionally, a landspout was observed in southern Beaverhead County near the Idaho border.
episodes.183048: A complex of thunderstorms clipped far southern Nebraska during the evening of August 5th. The vast majority of the severe weather with this event in the NWS Hastings CWA occurred along and south of the Nebraska-Kansas state line. Scattered thunderstorms developed in a west to east orientation right along the state line between 7-8 PM CDT. Activity took on supercell characteristics from time to time (owing to moderate instability and increasing deep layer shear) and produced a couple instances of quarter size hail in Webster County. Thunderstorms shifted east and southeast of the area between 9-10 PM CDT.
episodes.183049: Widespread thunderstorms brought several instances of large hail and damaging winds to north central Kansas during the evening of August 8th. Initial thunderstorm development occurred during the late afternoon hours in northwest Kansas before shifting eastward during the evening. The first severe thunderstorm arrived in western Phillips County as a supercell shortly before 8 PM CDT. The worst part of the storm continued northeast along Highway 283 and produced large hail and damaging wind gusts around 70 MPH in the Long Island vicinity before weakening as it moved into NW Smith County. Additional severe thunderstorms, including both supercells and bowing line segments, moved into western Rooks County between 8-9 PM CDT. This is where the most intense severe weather in the NWS Hastings CWA occurred with this event. Several instances of severe wind gusts were observed, including significant severe gusts of 75 to 80 MPH. Thunderstorms continued east across remaining portions of north central Kansas between 9-10 PM, but gusts in these areas remained sub-severe in the 50 to 55 MPH range.
episodes.183090: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust along the Brevard Coast near Cape Canaveral.
episodes.183091: A thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud in Indian River County.
episodes.183135: A heavy rain event in early August pushed the James River near Huron back into Minor Flood Stage for much of the month. Impacts were limited to minor agriculture flooding.
episodes.183143: Scattered strong to severe convection moved from the High Plains into portions of northern and eastern Oklahoma during the early morning of the 6th. Increased storm organization, into small lines, aided in a few damaging wind outcomes across the area.
episodes.183319: Anomalous moisture and a vigorous shortwave caused a semi-continuous line of thunderstorms that brought heavy rainfall across north-central Idaho.
episodes.183649: A fading MCS system moved southward across SE GA in the early evening where the system encountered high low-level instability. Strong wind gusts produced some damage.
episodes.183650: A fading MCS system moved southward across SE GA in the early evening where the system encountered high low-level instability. Strong wind gusts produced some damage.
episodes.183929: Showers and thunderstorms percolated through much of the day along a stationary boundary over northwest Iowa. By evening a more robust shortwave moved across the area, accompanied by 30 kts of shear and 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE. This allowed for storms to strengthen across west central Iowa with gusty winds producing some minor damage to trees and out buildings. Additionally, due to the orientation of the shear, a few weak tornadoes developed and were discovered using high resolution satellite imagery.
episodes.184030: Clusters of thunderstorms developed in eastern Nebraska as a mid-level low moved across the northern Plains. An EF-U tornado was reported near Snyder with no known impacts or damage. The highest measured wind gust was 62 mph in Gage County. There were a few reports of tree damage across the area.
episodes.184037: A weak shortwave trough moving through the Ohio Valley coincided with peak diurnal heating, ample atmospheric moisture, minor shear, and moderate downdraft potential. Scattered thunderstorms developed across Northwest Georgia and the Atlanta Metro, causing wind damage.
episodes.184506: A strong storm system and its attendant surface low moved across the area during the late afternoon and evening hours. This led to a tornado briefly touching down multiple times as a storm moved eastward near the town of La Harpe. The tornado was rated EF-U as there were no visible signs of damage.
episodes.184569: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a warm front produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.184579: During the afternoon of the 5th a couple of storms formed in the southwest Texas Panhandle. One of these storm tracked across parts of Amarillo and dropping hail between 1.00 and 1.25 in diameter. Later in the evening a cluster of storms formed in the far southeast corner of Colorado and moved southeast through the western Oklahoma Panhandle and traveled southeast through the north central and eastern portions of the Texas Panhandle. These storms produced 1 hail and several severe wind gusts measuring 58 to 75 mph.
episodes.184584: During the afternoon of the 5th a couple of storms formed in the southwest Texas Panhandle. One of these storm tracked across parts of Amarillo and dropping hail between 1.00 and 1.25 in diameter. Later in the evening a cluster of storms formed in the far southeast corner of Colorado and moved southeast through the western Oklahoma Panhandle and traveled southeast through the north central and eastern portions of the Texas Panhandle. These storms produced 1 hail and several severe wind gusts measuring 58 to 75 mph.
episodes.184586: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the northwest central Virginia to the south of a stationary front draped across northern Virginia into central West Virginia. By early afternoon, a surface trough had developed along the lee side of the Blue Ridge Mountains, providing the lower atmospheric convergence needed to aid in thunderstorm development. Surface-based CAPE values were estimated to be in the 1,500 to 2,000 J/Kg range by noon just east of the Blue Ridge, while precipitable water values had risen into the 1.7 inch to 1.8 inch range, both of which supported heavy downpours and wet microbursts. A couple of the storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds which downed trees.
episodes.184587: Showers and thunderstorms developed across northwest North Carolina to the south of a stationary front draped across northern Virginia into central West Virginia.  By early afternoon, a surface trough had developed along the lee side of the Blue Ridge Mountains, providing the lower atmospheric convergence needed to aid in thunderstorm development.  A couple of the storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds which downed trees, while flash flooding occurred with one slow-moving storm that produced an estimated 4 to 5 inches of rainfall within a 2-hour period.
episodes.184619: A vigorous short-wave trough interacted with an approaching low pressure system and associated warm frontal boundary to trigger clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms across west-central Illinois during the late afternoon of August 6th.  Due to enhanced low-level wind shear along and north of the warm front, many of the cells began rotating and spinning up occasional funnel clouds.  One of the cells intensified as it pushed into Sangamon County, producing a long-track tornado that was on the ground for over 25 miles from just north of Pawnee in far southeastern Sangamon County to southeast of Stonington in Christian County.  The tornado produced EF-1 damage along much of its path, peaking with EF-2 damage just south of Willeys in Christian County.  This particular thunderstorm cell dropped 2-inch diameter hail north of Taylorville and went on to produce a downburst with 80 mph wind gusts in far eastern Shelby County near Lake Mattoon.  The storms eventually congealed into a line as they pushed into eastern Illinois later in the evening, with scattered wind damage, hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.184625: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184627: An active summer pattern led to scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced damaging winds. In addition, heavy rain in a short period of time led to isolated instances of flash flooding in Bay county.
episodes.184632: An active summer pattern led to scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, some of which produced damaging winds. In addition, heavy rain in a short period of time led to isolated instances of flash flooding in Lowndes county.
episodes.184645: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging straight-line winds over parts of Elbert, Lincoln, Weld and Washington counties.  The hail ranged in size from ping pong to tennis ball size.  In Weld County, intense straight-line winds downed two trees and flattened a nearby corn crop.
episodes.184648: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over parts of Douglas, Jefferson and Larimer counties.  The storms produced large hail ranging from nickel to quarter size.
episodes.184716: A complex of thunderstorms moved southeast into and across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 6th. The strongest thunderstorm produced small hail.
episodes.184830: A mesoscale convective vortex, originating from the Plains, moved into the Mid-South. This feature re-ignited convection during the afternoon hours across northeast Mississippi as the airmass destabilized due to surface heating. There were numerous reports of damaging winds across northeast Mississippi.
episodes.184921: A complex of severe thunderstorms moved through much of Central and South Central Kansas during evening hours of 5 August 2023.  There were numerous reports of winds in excess of 60 mph with some of the highest winds reported of 74 mph.  There were also numerous reports of trees down, power poles down, power outages and even a fire ignited by down power lines in the City of Wichita.
episodes.184926: An active northwest upper flow pattern produced several waves of convective storms during the first week of August.
episodes.184961: A complex of severe thunderstorms rolled through South Central and Southeast Kansas on the morning of 5 August.  Wind speeds up to 70 mph were reported with numerous reports of damage to trees and other minor property.  Very heavy rain was also reported with the heaviest train in Neosho and Montgomery county.
episodes.184987: After reports of over 3 inches of rain fell, water began to pool in urban areas in Cass and Clay counties. Numerous reports of flooding came in after an areal flood advisory was issued.
episodes.184988: After reports of over 3 inches of rain fell, water began to pool in urban areas in Cass and Clay counties. Numerous reports of flooding came in after an areal flood advisory was issued.
episodes.184999: A couple thunderstorms moved east through Yuma County during the afternoon.  Hail up to golf ball size and wind gusts up to 64 MPH were reported with these storms.
episodes.185000: A cluster of thunderstorms moved eastward across Northwest Kansas.  Hail up to lime size and wind gusts up to 110 MPH were reported with these storms.  The strongest storms were over Graham and Norton counties.  The storm in Almena area was particularly intense in which mature tree trunks were snapped among other damage.
episodes.185008: A cluster of thunderstorms moved across Southwest Nebraska.  Hail up to quarter size and wind gusts up to 69 MPH were reported with these storms.
episodes.185130: The one and only time this year when there was a proper monsoonal tap over southern Colorado. In this case, there was weak northweserly flow aloft, and southeasterly flow at the surface, which resulted in a unstable and high shear environment. There was almost a tornado that touched down, however, no reports of debris or damage were reported.
episodes.185223: Scattered storms along a front caused severe wind gusts late on 8/5 and into 8/6.
episodes.185279: An outflow boundary from earlier day convection focused a gradient of instability and storm development with additional destabilization from heating by early afternoon. Boundary interactions from sluggish storms led to training of heavy rainfall cores and localized flash flooding.
episodes.185348: A mid-level shortwave trough tracking eastward led to the development of scattered showers and storms over the western to eastern Piedmont of central North Carolina in the early evening hours. This led to several damaging wind reports. Storm coverage weakened with eastward extent over the Coastal Plain.
episodes.185364: An area of showers and thunderstorms moved across the North Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon. Some of the embedded storms became briefly severe, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185365: An area of showers and thunderstorms moved across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. Some of the embedded storms became briefly severe, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.186578: A mesoscale convective complex caused severe thunderstorms to develop in west central, south central, and southwest Illinois during the afternoon and evening hours of August 6th. There were numerous reports of severe hail up to 1.50 and a few reports of severe wind gusts.
episodes.186587: Several gale-force peak convective wind gusts impacted the OH and PA shore of Lake Erie on August 6th and 10th. During the early afternoon through early evening of the 6th, a surface low drifted northeastward from northwestern OH to Lake St. Clair. The low became occluded as the trailing cold front moved eastward from far-western OH to central OH and a nearly-stationary front lingered near the Lake Erie shore in north-central and northeast OH. Isolated to scattered multicell thunderstorms persisted generally northeastward across far-northern OH and Lake Erie during the late afternoon through early evening after developing along the occluded and nearly-stationary fronts. These storms occurred along a tight gradient of MUCAPE and in a region of weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear.  ||Several days later, a cold front drifted generally southward across southern ON and southern Lower MI to northern Lake Erie during the early afternoon through early evening of the 10th. Isolated to scattered multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted generally southeastward across Lake Erie after developing along the front. The storms persisted amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.

A tornado touched down 3 miles north of Pawnee at 6:09 PM CDT.  It caused minor roof damage and blew down several trees before it crossed into Christian County just north of the intersection of Pawnee-New City Road and Skaggs Road at 6:13 PM CDT.

This tornado crossed from Sangamon County into far western Christian County just north of the intersection of Pawnee-New City Road and Skaggs Road at 6:13 PM CDT.  It continued east-southeastward across Sangchris Lake, damaging a home near the lakeshore and causing extensive tree damage before passing just north of Tovey and Kincaid.  The tornado crossed Route 29 southeast of Sharpsburg and tracked over mainly open fields between Routes 29 and 48.  It then strengthened and caused EF-2 damage 2 miles south of Willeys along 1600 East Road just south of 1600 North Road where it demolished about 2/3 of a house.  The tornado continued east-southeastward, then dissipated near North 2300 East Road about a half mile north of 1500 North Road at 7:03 PM CDT.
